clue.text: Name for hill in Rome in a Latin exam, initially — under pressure

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places the rest of the wordplay below the abbreviation for pressure

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the first letter of exam

explanation.surface: A student must name one of Rome's hills in a pressured Latin exam.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down clue P sits on top, with A LATIN E beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Palatine is one of the seven hills on which ancient Rome was built.

clue.text: Fateful day in Senate that is ending early

indicators.note: ending early means the phrase stops one letter short of its proper finish

parts.note: id est is the Latin for that is, abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: A historical note on the day in the Senate that ended a ruler's life early.
explanation.walkthrough: Lop the last letter off id est to leave IDES.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ides of March was the day Julius Caesar was stabbed at a meeting of the Roman Senate.

clue.text: Measures section of totem, possibly

indicators.note: a section is a slice cut out of a longer run of text

parts.note: the letters run across the end of totem and the start of possibly

explanation.surface: Someone sizes up part of what may be a totem pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempos are the rates or speeds at which music is played, measures of its pace.

clue.text: Destruction of Capitol that's newsworthy

indicators.note: a building's destruction leaves its parts scattered, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Wrecking the Capitol building would certainly make the news.
explanation.walkthrough: The Capitol is the US Congress building in Washington, and also the temple of Jupiter on Rome's Capitoline Hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Something topical concerns current affairs, so it is of interest to the news.

clue.text: Leader in Congress introducing a law about cigarette problem in fall

indicators.note: the first piece introduces what follows, coming before it
the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of Congress

indicators.note: about means going round, so the law phrase wraps around the cigarette substance

parts.note: an act is a law passed by a legislature
tar is the harmful residue in cigarette smoke
taken as written

explanation.surface: A congressional leader brings in a law on the problem of smoking, which then fails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Problem' tempts as the eye-disease definition, but it belongs to the cigarette; the definition is 'fall', as in waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A cataract is a large, steep waterfall, so a fall of water.

clue.text: Like some senators, protest 50% of Arctic being taken over

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken over means flipped upside down, so the stated half reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a demo is a demonstration, a public protest
the word whose first half, three letters of six, is turned round

explanation.surface: Senators protest about part of the Arctic being taken over.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first half of Arctic is turned; the second half stays as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Democratic senators are members of the US Democratic Party, one of the two big parties in the Senate.

clue.text: Bottle used as weapon by Clint Eastwood

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a wine bottle holding twice the standard amount
second meaning: the .44 revolver carried by Eastwood's Dirty Harry

explanation.surface: In a bar brawl a bottle becomes a weapon in Clint Eastwood's hands.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an oversized wine bottle and a powerful handgun cartridge or revolver.

clue.text: Polish bilingual Brendan follows in US city

indicators.note: follows puts the setter's self-reference after the word for polish

parts.note: to sand is to smooth or polish
Brendan is the setter, who names himself twice: I in English and EGO in Latin

explanation.surface: A Polish speaker with two languages, named Brendan, lives in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' reads as the nationality, but it is the verb meaning to smooth. Ego is Latin for I.
explanation.definitionFit: San Diego is a large city in southern California.

clue.text: Name in hood for stadium

indicators.note: in places one item inside the neighbourhood word

parts.note: hood is slang for neighbourhood, a local area
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A gang names its neighbourhood after the local stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed venue for sport or shows, much like a stadium.

clue.text: God is object of American missions

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Roman god of war
second meaning: the planet NASA sends rovers and orbiters to

explanation.surface: Missionaries from America set out to spread the word of God.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missions' suggests religious missionaries, which the word God encourages; the missions are space flights.
explanation.definitionFit: The red planet is named after the Roman war god and has been explored by many US space probes.

clue.text: Diva and demure megastar sharing male

indicators.note: sharing means the two words overlap on one letter for male instead of each having its own copy

parts.note: prim means demure or proper
Madonna is the pop megastar

explanation.surface: A diva and a modest superstar share the same leading man.
explanation.walkthrough: The M ending one word starts the other, so it is written once; M is the abbreviation for male.
explanation.definitionFit: A prima donna is the leading female singer in an opera, the classic diva.

clue.text: Place for events in Rome, mainly about America

indicators.note: mainly means most but not all, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: circa is Latin for about, used with dates
US is the United States

explanation.surface: Where Rome's events were held, approximately like America's venues.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman circus, like the Circus Maximus, was an arena for chariot races and public games.

clue.text: Crazy outing in Rome or New York, say, in touching relationship

indicators.note: in places the scrambled trip inside the metropolis

parts.note: Rome and New York are examples of a city

indicators.note: crazy means disordered, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wild excursion in Rome or New York leads to a close relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled trip goes between the first letter of CITY and the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Contiguity is the state of being in contact or adjoining, things that touch.

clue.text: Lone answer for New Orleans, more for Rome, for instance?

definitions.text: Lone answer for New Orleans, more for Rome, for instance?

parts.note: surface reading: someone gives a single reply in place of a city
setter's reading: the letters of lone answer rearrange to New Orleans, and the letters of more rearrange to Rome; these are examples of letter swaps

explanation.surface: One reply stands for New Orleans and a bigger one for Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: Count the letters: 'lone answer' and 'New Orleans' use the same ten, 'more' and 'Rome' the same four.
explanation.definitionFit: Each pair consists of words made by rearranging the same letters, which is exactly the device being named.

clue.text: One bishop of Rome, like all associated with pride

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Pope Leo IX, read out as the answer
second meaning: lion-like, since a group of lions is a pride

explanation.surface: A proud bishop of Rome resembles everyone linked with pride.
explanation.walkthrough: Popes are bishops of Rome; the Roman numeral IX is spoken as nine.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonine means of or like a lion, and a pride is the collective noun for lions.

clue.text: Closely observe what's cut in middle of Corn Belt

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Latin instruction to note well

definitions.text: what's cut in middle of Corn Belt
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the full phrase whose shortened form NB stands in the middle of corN Belt

explanation.surface: Pay attention to what gets harvested in the heart of the Corn Belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' suggests harvesting corn, but it means abbreviated; the cut-down form sits in the centre of the two words. The Corn Belt is the US Midwest farming region.
explanation.definitionFit: Nota bene is Latin for note well, used in writing to tell the reader to pay close attention.

clue.text: Something created by senators, say, covering half of Utah

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so the speech verb surrounds the state fragment

parts.note: to state is to say
the first two of Utah's four letters

explanation.surface: Senators, for instance, draft laws covering part of Utah.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like the 'for example' marker after senators, but it is the verb to state.
explanation.definitionFit: A statute is a written law passed by a legislature such as a senate.

clue.text: Dulles or JFK, for example, spoke for forum, finally, in broken Latin

indicators.note: something broken is smashed into pieces that can be put back in another order
finally picks the closing letter of each of the three words before it

parts.note: the last letters of spoke, for and forum
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone at a US airport addresses a forum in poor Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Dulles and JFK are airports, and a terminal is the building where flights arrive and depart, so by extension the airport itself.

clue.text: Sam, for example, a Republican? That's iffy

parts.note: Uncle Sam personifies the US
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: Is Uncle Sam a Republican? Hard to say.
explanation.definitionFit: Something iffy is doubtful or uncertain, not clear-cut.

clue.text: Musical politician in Latin home, mostly rebuilt

indicators.note: rebuilt means put together again in a different form
mostly means all but a little, so the last letter goes

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A politician fond of musicals rebuilds his Latin-style house.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Hamilton was a US Founding Father whose life became a hit stage musical.

clue.text: Helps a number of Romans over troubles also engulfing part of US

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the Roman number on top of the rest

parts.note: taken as written
V is the Roman numeral for five
ails means troubles or afflicts
a second, parallel route: troubles also wrap round VA, the abbreviation for Virginia; it adds no further letters

explanation.surface: Romans help America with its problems.
explanation.walkthrough: Brendan gives two routes to one answer: A V over the word for troubles, or that same word wrapped round Virginia's state abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To avail is to be of use or help, so avails means helps.

clue.text: Slangily eliminate Republican in company, a noted speaker

indicators.note: in puts the killing and party pieces inside the word for company

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
to ice is slang for to kill
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A gangster in the firm bumps off a Republican orator.
explanation.definitionFit: Cicero was the great orator of ancient Rome, famous for his speeches in the Senate.

clue.text: Grieves about middle of Louisiana and perilous times

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the weeping verb goes round the chosen letter

parts.note: to cry is to grieve or weep

indicators.note: middle of picks the single central letter of a nine-letter word

parts.note: the fifth of the nine letters of Louisiana

explanation.surface: Someone mourns over Louisiana's hard times, perhaps after a hurricane.
explanation.definitionFit: Crises are times of intense danger or difficulty.

clue.text: I'll be upset after start of conflict, since America is what produces it

indicators.note: after puts the shuffled phrase at the end, behind the other pieces
the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of conflict

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disarranged

parts.note: as means since, as in because
US is the United States
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone vows to be upset once a conflict starts, since America is behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'it' of the definition is the conflict already named in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A casus belli, Latin for occasion of war, is the act or event that justifies or provokes a war.

clue.text: Part of Star Wars character with little time for final notice

parts.note: the first part of Obi-Wan Kenobi's name
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A Star Wars character's brief screen time earns a last mention.
explanation.definitionFit: An obit, short for obituary, is the newspaper notice published after a death.

clue.text: Sex in party set up for poet

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the party word
in a down clue, set up means raised so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a do is a party
sex is Latin for six, VI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A party is arranged around sex for a racy poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sex' looks like the racy surface but is Latin for six, so it is a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovid was a Roman poet, author of the Metamorphoses and the Art of Love.

clue.text: Reconstructed Incan material one found in Peru, say

indicators.note: reconstructed means built again in a different shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Rebuilt Inca remains are found in Peru, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: The Incas built their empire in Peru, so the surface ties together nicely.
explanation.definitionFit: Peru is a country of South America, so someone from there is a Latin American.

clue.text: See 25
